source_citation.quote: **Retention — Card 2 item 2.c, DL-424 (review round 7).** Project-scoped `filesafe.destructive_override_requested` is permanent proof of the request, refusal or failure: `retention_policy_ref = RP-AUTHORITY-INDEFINITE`, reusing the exact existing Storage registry object (indefinite, no TTL or count limit, fail_closed overflow, hold_eligible, no expiry action). It never expires by age or count, remains inspectable after seven years, and survives deletion of the file or chat it describes. Only explicit **Delete Puppet Master project data** removes this Project history under existing authorization, deletion and protection rules; **Remove project from list** does not delete that data. If space runs out, refuse new entries instead of dropping old ones. Supporting approvals, source snapshots and recovery logs retain their own lifetimes; permanent EventRecord proof grants no access to a deleted or inaccessible linked body. Jared answered "i approve all of it"; the presented deck maps approve all to option A. The accepted answer is landed in `Plans/Decision_Log.md#DL-424` (batch 1); this unit applies its exact option A and shared conditions. This applies exactly item 2.c and Card 2's shared conditions. It adds no counting or deletion rule for future entries outside Projects. **Application scope remains PENDING_RETENTION_DECISION and may not record this event until exact approved rules exist.** Exact remaining question: What counting scope, capacity/overflow behavior and deletion/protection rules govern application-scoped `filesafe.destructive_override_requested` history? A Project policy must not be inferred for it. No original body, snapshot, transaction, generic index or checkpoint lifetime is reopened.
